iṇa: iṇa (nt.) [Sk. ṛṇa, see also P. an--aṇa] debt D I.71, 73; A III.352; V.324 (enumd. with baddha, jāni & kali); Sn 120; J I.307; II.388, 423; III.66; IV.184 (iṇagga for nagga?); 256; V.253 (where enumd. as one of the 4 paribhogas, viz. theyya°, iṇa°, dāya°, sāmi°); VI.69, 193; Miln 375; PvA 273, 276, iṇaṃ gaṇhāti to borrow money or take up a loan Vism 556; SnA 289; PvA 3. -- iṇaṃ muñcati to discharge a debt J IV.280; V.238; °ṃ sodheti same PvA 276; labhati same PvA 3.--apagama absence of debt ThA 245. --gāhaka a borrower Miln 364. --ghāta stricken by debt Sn 246 (= iṇaṃ gahetva tassa appadānena iṇaghāta). --ṭṭha (with iṇaṭṭa as v. l. at all passages, see aṭṭa) fallen into or being in debt M I.463 = S III.93 = It 89 = Miln 279. --paṇṇa promissory note J I.230; IV.256. --mokkha release from debt J IV.280; V.239. --sādhaka negotiator of a loan Miln 365.
iṇāyika: iṇāyika [fr. iṇa] one connected with a debt, viz. (1) a creditor S I.170; J IV.159, 256; VI.178; ThA 271 see also dhanika); PvA 3. -- (2) a debtor Vin I.76; Nd1 160.
